# Server hooks

<!-- generated by misc/insanotic/gen-lua-hooks.sh; do not edit by hand -->

Every hook the 0.8.6 server game code exposes through `MUTATOR_HOOKABLE`,
with its arguments and return semantics. Lua plugins subscribe with
`xon.on("<HookName>", function(ev) ... end)`.

## How hooks behave

- Arguments live in the QuakeC globals `MUTATOR_ARGV_<n>_<type>`. In Lua they
  are `ev[n]` (the same index `n`), and `ev.hook` is the hook name.
- **in** arguments are read when the hook fires. **out** arguments are
  written back after all handlers ran: assign `ev[n] = value` to change
  them. An argument listed as both in and out arrives with the current value
  and can be modified.
- Return value: the game ORs together the return values of every
  callback (QuakeC mutators and Lua handlers). Each hook below says whether
  its call sites use that result; where they do, `true` means what the
  description says (usually "block" or "handled") and `false`/`nil`
  keeps the default behaviour.
- Entities are handles (`nil` for world/none); vectors are `xon.vec`
  tables; `bool` arguments are Lua booleans; `int` arguments are integers.
- Handlers run in plugin load order, then in registration order within a plugin.
  Each plugin sees the out-values left by the previous plugin.

Hooks that some gamemode claims with `CBC_ORDER_EXCLUSIVE` cannot have
extra callbacks and are **not forwarded to Lua**: `Bot_FixCount`, `TeamBalance_CheckAllowedTeams`.

165 hooks. Source paths are relative to `qcsrc/`.

Return value: **used**: the game checks the combined result (see the description for what `true` does).

| ev | dir | type | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | in | entity | player |
| 1 | in | bool | is_forced |

### TeamBalance_CheckAllowedTeams

Allows adjusting allowed teams. Return true to use the bitmask value and set non-empty string to use team entity name. Both behaviors can be active at the same time and will stack allowed teams.

_Not forwarded to Lua (exclusive hook)._

Return value: **used**: the game checks the combined result (see the description for what `true` does).

| ev | dir | type | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | in | float | mask of teams |
| 0 | out | float |  |
| 1 | in | string | team entity name |
| 1 | out | string |  |
| 2 | in | entity | player checked |

### SV_ParseClientCommand

called when a client command is parsed NOTE: hooks MUST start with if (MUTATOR_RETURNVALUE) return false; NOTE: return true if you handled the command, return false to continue handling NOTE: THESE HOOKS MUST NEVER EVER CALL tokenize() // example: MUTATOR_HOOKFUNCTION(foo_SV_ParseClientCommand) { if (MUTATOR_RETURNVALUE) // command was already handled? return false; if (cmd_name == "echocvar" && cmd_argc >= 2) { print(cvar_string(argv(1)), "\n"); return true; } if (cmd_name == "echostring" && cmd_argc >= 2) { print(substring(cmd_string, argv_start_index(1), argv_end_index(-1) - argv_start_index(1)), "\n"); return true; } return false; }

Return value: **used**: the game checks the combined result (see the description for what `true` does).

| ev | dir | type | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | in | entity | client sending the command |
| 1 | in | string | command name |
| 2 | in | int | argc (also, argv() can be used) |
| 3 | in | string | whole command, use only if you really have to |

|---|---|---|---|

| 1 | in | int | argc (also, argv() can be used) |
| 2 | in | string | whole command, use only if you really have to |
